who: Historian of modern France at the University of Rochester, 1970–1988; PhD Cornell 1963.

evidence.says: The department history lists Sanford Harold Elwitt with a Cornell PhD in 1963 and Rochester faculty service in 1970–1988.
The AHA obituary identifies Rochester historian Sanford Elwitt as the author of The Third Republic Defended and records his Cornell doctorate.
The authority for Elwitt, Sanford cites The Third Republic defended (1986) under his name.

notes: Doctorate and Rochester appointment match; the shared book connects the LC candidate to that historian.

who: Historian of the American West at the University of New Mexico, 1979–2001; PhD Oregon 1966.

evidence.says: UNM identifies Richard W. Etulain as professor emeritus, with an Oregon PhD and UNM teaching service from 1979 to 2001; publications include Calamity Jane: A Reader's Guide (2015).
His contributor biography gives an Oregon PhD in 1966 and UNM teaching in 1979–2001.
The Richard W. Etulain authority includes Richard Etulain as a name variant and cites Calamity Jane (2015).

notes: Name variants, doctorate, university and teaching period agree with the supervisor record.

who: U.S. labor historian at Northern Illinois University; PhD Washington University in St. Louis 1997.

evidence.says: NIU lists Rosemary Feurer as professor, gives her Washington University, St. Louis PhD (1997), and lists Radical Unionism in the Midwest, 1900–1950 (2006).
The collection biography records the 1997 Washington University PhD and says Feurer began teaching at NIU in 1995.
The Rosemary Feurer authority is established from Radical unionism in the Midwest, 1900–1950 (2006).

notes: Exact doctorate and NIU career agree; the same book identifies the authority candidate.

who: Historian of western Canada and labor at the University of Manitoba; PhD history, Toronto 1974.

evidence.says: Manitoba lists Gerald Friesen as distinguished professor emeritus of history, with a Toronto history PhD in 1974; publications include The Canadian Prairies and A Guide to the Study of Manitoba Local History.
The university's 2024 account describes Friesen's Toronto doctoral research and his completed forty-year teaching career at Manitoba.
The Gerald Friesen authority cites The Canadian prairies (1984) and A guide to the study of Manitoba local history (1981).

notes: The doctorate and long Manitoba career agree; two shared works establish the candidate identity.

who: Historian of modern Spain at Claremont Graduate University since 2009; PhD history, UCLA 1999.

evidence.says: Goode's institutional CV records a UCLA history PhD in 1999, CGU employment beginning in 2009, and Impurity of Blood: Defining Race in Spain, 1870–1930 (2009).
CGU identifies Joshua Goode as professor of cultural studies and history, specializing in modern Spain, and lists his UCLA doctorate and Impurity of Blood.
The Joshua Goode authority cites Impurity of blood (2009) under his name.

notes: The exact PhD year, appointment period and shared book support the match.

who: Environmental historian at the University of Kansas; PhD Columbia 2004.

evidence.says: KU's biography identifies Sara Gregg as a Kansas history and environmental studies faculty member, gives her Columbia PhD in 2004, and names Managing the Mountains (2010) as her first book.
The 2017 fellowship biography identifies Gregg as associate professor of history and environmental studies at Kansas, with a Columbia PhD, and dates her move to Kansas to 2010.
The Sara M. Gregg authority cites Managing the mountains (2010), whose title page gives that name.

notes: Doctorate and Kansas employment fit the student years; the shared book connects Sara Gregg to Sara M. Gregg.

who: Historian of U.S. foreign relations at Bowling Green State University; PhD Virginia 1965.

evidence.says: BGSU identifies Dr. Gary R. Hess as distinguished research professor emeritus, gives his Virginia PhD in 1965, and lists The United States at War, 1941–1945 among his books.
BGSU's 2009 retirement announcement includes history professor Gary Hess among its distinguished research professors receiving emeritus status.
The Gary R. Hess authority cites The United States at war, 1941–1945 (1986), explicitly identifying the author with Bowling Green State University.

notes: Exact doctorate and explicit LC university affiliation establish the match; the later student completions fall after his 2009 retirement.

who: Military and diplomatic historian at Mississippi State, 1965–1988; PhD Texas 1964, subsequently at VMI.

evidence.says: VMI's September 2, 1988 faculty announcement identifies D. Clayton James as a military and diplomatic historian arriving after 23 years at Mississippi State, with a University of Texas PhD in 1964.
The D. Clayton James authority cites Command crisis (1982), explicitly identifying its author with Mississippi State University.
The alternate Daniel James authority describes a Latin American historian with a London School of Economics doctorate in 1979 and an Indiana appointment beginning in 1999.
Daniel James's institutional biography identifies his Oxford and London School of Economics education, Argentina-focused social and labor history, and U.S. teaching at Yale, Duke and Indiana.

notes: p-135246 matches the doctorate and Mississippi State period. Reject p-253 (Daniel James): its doctorate, field and career identify a different historian.
